novelty_flags.label: comparator_promise_table / BacchiocchiBastianinKitagawaMirto2024PartialHSVAR
novelty_flags.one_line: The claim that Theorems 1--3 characterize point and set identification inside repeated-eigenvalue rotation blocks is inaccurate: those results address sign/permutation, distinct-eigenvalue point identification, and eigen-decomposition; set identification under multiplicity is developed later.

soundness_flags.label: ass:nonnegative-variance-shifts
soundness_flags.one_line: BACKSHIFT assumes diagonal covariance shifts, not that every target variance increment is nonnegative relative to one fixed observed baseline; retag this as a novel baseline-minimum design restriction and justify it.

soundness_flags.label: ass:reference-shifts-all-targets
soundness_flags.one_line: BACKSHIFT's profile condition does not require a distinguished environment with strictly positive increment at every target; retag and motivate this reference-panel condition rather than calling it standard.

soundness_flags.label: thm:consistency-above-boundary
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed finite-sample threshold omits a triangle-inequality term: on ||hatθ-θ||w≤cα, the 1-approximate selector can satisfy ||tildeθn-θ||w<2cα+1, so sqrt(2)mδn>cα+1 does not exclude an opposite-class selected point.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes diagonal covariance shifts and its uniqueness condition is noncollinearity of the vector of covariance differences; it permits an observational baseline only as an alternative convention and does not impose nonnegative increments from a fixed baseline or one reference changing every target.

Theorem 2 characterizes LIT's candidate set as children of changing exogenous noises in an auxiliary graph and explicitly establishes that it is a superset of the observed true targets under latent confounding.
Pairwise noncollinearity/nonzero variance-signal vectors yields uniqueness of the mixing matrix up to permutation and rescaling after covariance differencing.
The paper imposes separability/recoverability of the mixing matrix and proves a correspondence between SEM-ME and latent-root models, rather than a covariance-only realization converse.

Theorem 1 handles sign normalization and column permutation; Theorem 2 gives point identification under distinct diagonal terms; Theorem 3 gives an eigen-decomposition representation. Multiplicity/set-identification analysis is subsequent material.
Theorem 1 constructs an asymptotic test-inversion confidence set for a bivariate total causal effect while retaining two possible linear causal structures.
Theorems 2.3--2.4 give uniform asymptotic coverage for identified sets and functions/images of those sets under their inversion construction.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economics and Statistics 104(3), version-of-record PDF
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 supplies a robust chi-square K-statistic for heteroskedastic identification, and the paper frames near-proportional variance changes as weak identification.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair Theorem 5 using the selector bound ||tildeθn-θ||w<2||hatΣ-θ||w+1, then restate the explicit threshold and probability bound; alternatively choose an epsilon_n selector and make its contribution explicit.

Retag the fixed-baseline one-sided shifts and all-target reference environment as novel design restrictions, give a realistic panel-design justification, and add a signed-shift or no-common-reference boundary result showing exactly what the certificate loses.

Replace the Bacchiocchi theorem-number claim with the actual multiplicity/set-identification theorem locations and add a direct comparison theorem showing why acyclic labeled fibers are stricter than their rotation sets.

recommended_next_step: Revise the selector-dependent finite-sample boundary and the two mislabelled intervention assumptions, then rerun novelty review with corrected Bacchiocchi locations.
